sheet-1.description: The lower half of sheet 1 is the only part of the atlas drawn at 50 feet to an inch and shows the business centre of Little Falls around the meeting of Main Street, Stevens Avenue and the Little Falls Turnpike. Main Street runs down the middle of the part from Stevens Avenue at the top to Lincoln Avenue at the bottom, with Stanley along the left edge and Maple Avenue across the lower right corner; the Little Falls Turnpike leaves Main Street towards the right, and the Morris Canal crosses the upper right beside the heavy line that separates this map from the key map. The frontage of Main Street between Stevens Avenue and the turnpike is the densest commercial block of the township: a bank, a drug store and a row of stores on the west side, and on the east side stores, the Eagle Hotel and the Enterprise Hose Company No. 2 fire house next to a large garage. Further down are the Reformed Church with its parish house, horse sheds and auto stalls, an undertaker, a carpenter shop, a battery station and a plumber, among frame dwellings on deep lots. Fire alarm boxes, hydrants and six-inch water pipes are marked in the streets. The upper half of the sheet, left out of this part, holds the key map of the whole township at 1000 feet to an inch, the index of streets and specials, and notes on water supply and the fire department.
notes: Little Falls Turnpike is now Paterson Avenue.
Stanley is today's Stanley Street; Maple Avenue is today's Maple Street.
Main Street / Paterson Avenue was hand-picked; the detector found Main / Stevens, Main / Lincoln and Lincoln / Stanley.

Scale 50 ft to an inch (main map). Top half is the key map of the township (1000 ft to an inch), index and water/fire notes, left out of the mask. Main map: Main Street from Stevens Avenue to Lincoln Avenue, Little Falls Turnpike (now Paterson Avenue), Stanley, Maple Avenue, Morris Canal; Reformed Church, Eagle Hotel, fire house. Main/Paterson hand-picked.

sheet-2-1.description: The main part of sheet 2 covers the southern half of the Singac section, between the Passaic River on the left and the county line with Essex County (Verona Township and North Caldwell) on the right, from the Pompton Turnpike along the top edge down to Lindsley Road and Clarence Avenue. Main Street crosses the part diagonally from the turnpike to the bottom edge. West of it the streets run down to Woodcliffe Avenue and the river: Stinson Place, Garrabrant Avenue, Riker Avenue, Micklejohn Avenue, Taylor Avenue, Fickett Avenue and River Boulevard (Riker), with Mozart Avenue and Orchard Avenue running south to Clarence Avenue. Boat houses line the river bank behind Woodcliffe Avenue, and an amusement ground near the bottom left has a roller coaster and a merry-go-round. East of Main Street the newer streets of the section are laid out at an angle: Amity, Veranda Avenue, Park Place, Coney Road, Stanley Road, Riker Road, Muzzy Road, Veazy, Henry Avenue and Fern Avenue, mostly in narrow lots with scattered frame dwellings, and at the top Van Pelt Place with Gray, Haines Place, Hughes Place, Weaver and Tolstoi Place running up to the turnpike. Institutions include Little Falls Public School No. 3 on Garrabrant Avenue, the Singac Firemen's Hall and Holy Angels church property near the turnpike, the Colonel Inn on Main Street, the Mondon's Hotel and a Russian Orthodox church. Large tracts (blocks 206, 207, 211) are left blank. The county and township boundaries cross the lower right.
notes: Pompton Turnpike is now Newark - Pompton Turnpike.
Fickett Avenue matches today's Pleasant Avenue; Orchard Avenue matches today's Cherry Street; Gray is today's Grey Street.
Stanley Road / Veranda and Amity / Veranda were rejected by the fit (10 to 15 m): Veranda Avenue north of Coney Road appears realigned.

Scale 100 ft. Singac section: Main Street, Pompton Turnpike (now Newark - Pompton Turnpike), Woodcliffe Av, Garrabrant, Riker, Micklejohn, Taylor, Fickett (now Pleasant Avenue), River Blvd (Riker), Mozart, Orchard (now Cherry Street), Amity, Veranda, Park Pl, Coney Rd, Stanley Rd, Lindsley Rd, Van Pelt Pl. Two parts: part 1 main map; part 2 inset at lower right (Clarence Av, Woodcliffe Av, Main, Fairfield Rd, now Little Falls Road), placed from three hand-picked junctions.

sheet-2-2.description: The inset in the lower right corner of sheet 2 continues the Singac section southwards across Clarence Avenue to the Fairfield Road, at the southern tip of the township where it meets North Caldwell in Essex County. It is framed by a heavy line and drawn at the same scale and angle as the main part, with its own north arrow. Woodcliffe Avenue runs down the left side between the Passaic River and the lots, Clarence Avenue crosses the top with the ends of Mozart Avenue and Orchard Avenue meeting it, Main runs down the right side past Hillside Avenue, and the Fairfield Road crosses the bottom along the county line. The block between them is cut into small numbered lots, about half built with frame dwellings, and a group of bath houses and lockers stands by the river at the lower left; a row of booths faces the Fairfield Road near Main. Hydrants and six-inch water pipes are marked in Clarence Avenue and Fairfield Road. The ground beyond the county line is left blank.
notes: Fairfield Road is today's Little Falls Road at this point.
Placed from three hand-picked junctions (Clarence / Woodcliffe, Clarence / Main, Main / Fairfield Road); an exact fit with no independent check.

Scale 100 ft. Two parts: part 1 main map; part 2 inset at lower right (Clarence Av, Woodcliffe Av, Main, Fairfield Rd, now Little Falls Road), placed from three hand-picked junctions.

sheet-3-1.description: The main part of sheet 3 shows the northern half of the Singac section, inside a loop of the Passaic River with Wayne Township and an island across the water. The river curves round the top of the part; Riverview Circle follows it, and below it a regular subdivision of very narrow lots is laid out along the Parkway, William and Louis, crossed by River, Little, Beauty Spot, Garden, Roselle, Arlington and Bogart. Only a scattering of these lots is built, mostly with small frame dwellings. At the upper right Island Avenue, Orchard and West End Avenue run between the river and Main Street, and Grey Rock Avenue enters at the right edge. The lower half is mostly open ground (block 40) crossed by the Erie Railroad's Greenwood Lake branch, with E. Woodcliffe along the river, the arbitrary courts M Ct, N Ct and Cholle, and near Main Street the E. L. Klotz lumber yard and the New Jersey Foundry Co. building drawn from plans. Along the bottom, between Arlington, Muller Place, Singac Place, Main and the Pompton Turnpike, stand stores, a garage, a dance hall, a hotel, Holy Angels Convent and School and the Singac fire department. Dewey Avenue and Grove reach the right edge. A public dock is marked on the river bank.
notes: The Arlington between Roselle and Bogart is today's Dairy Street; the Arlington near Pompton Turnpike keeps the name (Arlington Street).
Little is today's Lyttel Street; E. Woodcliffe is East Woodcliffe Avenue.
Main Street / William Street left out: the modern junction is about 14 m from the drawn one (Main Street realigned near the railroad).
The fitted scale is about 3 percent larger than the other 100 ft sheets.

Scale 100 ft. Singac section north of Main: Parkway, William, Louis, Garden, Roselle, Arlington (now Dairy Street), Bogart, Island Av, West End Av, Riverview Circle, Grove, Arlington and Muller Pl near Pompton Turnpike; Passaic River and island. Two parts: part 1 main map; part 2 inset at lower left (west side of Woodcliffe Av from Pompton Turnpike to Riker Av, drawn at another angle), helmert from three points along Woodcliffe Av.

sheet-3-2.description: The inset in the lower left corner of sheet 3 shows a strip of the Singac section between the Passaic River and Woodcliffe Avenue, from the Pompton Turnpike at the top to Riker Avenue at the bottom. It is separated from the main map by a heavy line and drawn at a different angle, with its own north arrow at the lower left. The strip continues the river frontage that sheet 2 shows only in part. At the top the Pompton Turnpike is lined with stores and dwellings; below it a boat house and lockers stand by the river, and a cluster of small cottages is set along A Court, an arbitrary name. Further down Stinson Place and Garrabrant Avenue end at Woodcliffe Avenue, which jogs between them, and the lots facing the river hold frame dwellings and a few outbuildings (blocks 9, 202 and 203). Riker Avenue is lettered along the bottom edge. The Passaic River runs down the left side of the inset.
notes: A Court is marked arbitrary on the sheet; it is not in today's street network.
Placed by a helmert fit from three points along Woodcliffe Avenue (Stinson, Garrabrant, Riker); low confidence.

Scale 100 ft. Singac section north of Main: Parkway, William, Louis, Garden, Roselle, Arlington (now Dairy Street), Bogart, Island Av, West End Av, Riverview Circle, Grove, Arlington and Muller Pl near Pompton Turnpike; Passaic River and island. Two parts: part 1 main map; part 2 inset at lower left (west side of Woodcliffe Av from Pompton Turnpike to Riker Av, drawn at another angle), helmert from three points along Woodcliffe Av.

sheet-4-1.description: Sheet 4 shows the eastern part of the Singac section between the Passaic River and the Pompton Turnpike. Main Street crosses the upper half diagonally; north of it Grey Rock Avenue, Orchard and Island Avenue run down to the river in narrow lots, and at the river the large buildings of the Beattie rug mills (shown in detail on the sheet 5 inset) occupy the frontage. South of Main Street are Woodside Avenue and Brookside Avenue, the yard of Robert C. Van Ness Inc., lumber and mason material, with lumber piles and sheds, and on the right Montclair Avenue and Union Avenue with St. Agnes Church and bowling alleys. The Erie Railroad's Greenwood Lake branch crosses the middle of the sheet, with the Singac Oil Co. storage plant on a siding. Below the railroad lies a subdivision of small lots on Dewey Avenue, Miles Avenue, Merritt Avenue, Grove Avenue, Wood, Van Ness, Woodhull Avenue and Strickland Avenue, and along the bottom Grove, 1st Street (Wausau), 2nd Street and 3rd Street run to the Pompton Turnpike. A large open tract (blocks 36 and 55) fills the lower right, bounded by the line between Verona Township and Essex County. The inset of Montclair Avenue at the lower right is not part of this map.
notes: Van Ness here is today's Bradford Avenue; Merritt Avenue is spelled Merrit Avenue today.
Pompton Turnpike is now Newark - Pompton Turnpike.
The railroad crossing of Montclair Avenue was rejected (4 m): the corridor may be drawn slightly off.

Scale 100 ft. Singac section: Main Street (Grey Rock, Orchard, Woodside, Brookside, Montclair, Union), Robert C. Van Ness lumber, Singac Oil Co, Dewey, Merritt, Wood, Van Ness (now Bradford Avenue), Woodhull, Strickland, Grove, 1st/2nd/3rd St, Pompton Turnpike; Beattie mill buildings at the top (shown on sheet 5 inset). Two parts: part 1 main map; part 2 inset at lower right (Montclair Av south of the railroad, blocks 55 and 62) not placed: no street junction drawn.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: Montclair Avenue south of the Erie Greenwood Lake branch (blocks 55 and 62, houses 78 to 103) (no street junction drawn; only lot lines along one street; needs parcel-corner control (step 6b) or carried points from a neighbour).

sheet-5-1.description: Sheet 5 covers the western end of the Little Falls centre, between the Passaic River and the abandoned Morris Canal at the top and the Verona Township line at the bottom. Main Street crosses the upper part from Union Avenue to the Stevens Avenue corner, where the stores of block 65 continue on sheet 1. North of Main the ground between the canal towpath and the street is open (block 58); south of it Warren, Walnut and Park run across to Center Avenue, Stevens Avenue and Ridge, and further down Prospect, Crane and Stanley complete the grid. Institutions include the Little Falls M. E. Church, the library, the municipal building with the fire department and Eagle Hose Co., Little Falls Public School No. 1 with its annex, and the New York Telephone Co. exchange; industry includes the Van Ness Lumber Co. yard, the C. W. Matches coal yard and, by the railroad, the machine works of Paul O. Abbe Inc. The Erie Railroad's Greenwood Lake branch crosses the lower half diagonally with the Little Falls passenger station, a freight house, a turntable and a round house. Proposed Street is drawn along the west side of block 57. A large blank area (blocks 61, 62 and 68) lies along the railroad. The inset of the Beattie mills at the lower left is a separate part.
notes: Park is now part of Walnut Street, which runs on from the old Walnut at Center Avenue.
The Morris Canal is marked abandoned, with the old tow path.
Proposed Street was not built under that name.

Scale 100 ft. Main Street from Union Av to Stevens Av, Warren, Walnut, Park (now Walnut Street), Prospect, Crane, Center Av, Stevens Av, Ridge Av; public school no. 1, municipal building, Erie Greenwood Lake branch with station and turntable, Paul O. Abbe machine works. Two parts: part 1 main map; part 2 inset at lower left (Beattie Mfg Co rug mills on Main Street between Montclair and Union Avs), helmert from two junctions on Main Street.

sheet-5-2.description: The inset at the lower left of sheet 5 shows the mills of the Beattie Mfg. Co., manufacturers of rugs, on the Passaic River between the river bank and Main Street, from the west end of the works to Union Avenue. It is framed by a heavy line and drawn at a smaller angle than the main map, with its own north arrow pointing up and to the left. The works fill almost the whole inset: printing, carding, dressing and printing, washing, drying, printing and winding, mixing, carding, twisting and spinning, weaving and weaving sizing and finishing buildings, a boiler room, a machine shop and an office, with a warehouse and a water tower near the west end. Automatic sprinklers are marked throughout. A note says that admittance was refused and that the information comes from the 1915 map with additional buildings drawn from the street. A dam and an old channel are drawn in the river behind the mill. Main runs along the bottom with hydrants and hose houses, Montclair Avenue meets it from below, and Union Avenue runs up the right side.
notes: The Beattie mill buildings also appear, undescribed, at the top of sheet 4.
Placed by a helmert fit from Main Street / Montclair Avenue (hand-picked) and Main Street / Union Avenue; low confidence.

Scale 100 ft. Main Street from Union Av to Stevens Av, Warren, Walnut, Park (now Walnut Street), Prospect, Crane, Center Av, Stevens Av, Ridge Av; public school no. 1, municipal building, Erie Greenwood Lake branch with station and turntable, Paul O. Abbe machine works. Two parts: part 1 main map; part 2 inset at lower left (Beattie Mfg Co rug mills on Main Street between Montclair and Union Avs), helmert from two junctions on Main Street.

sheet-6.description: Sheet 6 shows the regular residential grid east of the centre of Little Falls, between Ridge Avenue on the left and Wilmore Road, the old Cedar Grove Avenue, which follows the abandoned Morris Canal and its tow path along the upper right. The avenues run up the sheet (Ridge, Lincoln, 1st, 2nd, 3rd and 4th) and the streets across it (Stanley, Frances, Park, Prospect, Crane, which is also lettered 3rd Street, and a 3rd Street further down between 1st and 2nd Avenues). Most blocks are cut into narrow lots and are partly built with frame dwellings, with a few stores and garages; the Reformed Church parish property is at Stanley and Ridge. Blocks 77A and 78A at the lower left are laid out but nearly empty. The lower right is a large open tract (blocks 106 and 107), and the Erie Railroad's Greenwood Lake branch crosses the lower left corner. The Verona Township and Essex County line runs along the bottom.
notes: Frances is today's Francis Street; Park is now Walnut Street.
The 3rd Street between 1st and 2nd Avenues is today's Elm Street.
The Morris Canal is marked abandoned.

Scale 100 ft. Grid east of the centre: Stanley, Frances (now Francis Street), Park (now Walnut Street), Prospect, Crane (3rd St), 3rd St (now Elm Street) against Ridge, Lincoln, 1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th Avs and Wilmore Rd (Cedar Grove Av) along the abandoned Morris Canal. Pilot sheet.

sheet-7-1.description: The west part of sheet 7 covers the northern end of the township along the Little Falls Turnpike, which runs up the sheet beside the Passaic River towards Paterson. Between the turnpike and the Newark Water Supply and East Jersey Water Co. rights of way along the top, a subdivision of narrow lots is laid out on Maple, Ryle, Jackson and Willow Place, crossed by Harrison, Cedar (Centre) and Oak Place, with only a few dwellings built. Below it a large tract (block 94) is mostly open, and at the bottom Sindle Avenue and Van Ness Avenue run past two ponds to the Little Falls Washing Co. works and the Brookside Laundry, which has its own power and light plant, with a few dwellings along Sindle Avenue (block 89). The Little Falls Gun Club stands by the river. The top edge marks the Borough of East Paterson and refers to the Paterson atlas, volume three. A heavy line separates this part from the quarry tract and the Great Notch section on the right.
notes: Little Falls Turnpike is now Paterson Avenue; Maple is today's Madison Avenue; Jackson is Jackson Street; Willow Place is Willow Avenue.
Cedar Street / Jackson Street was excluded (narrow pair, 6 m residual).
See Map of Paterson, Volume Three, for the ground beyond the top edge.

Scale 100 ft. Two parts separated by a heavy line. Part 1: Little Falls Turnpike (now Paterson Avenue) by the Passaic, Maple (now Madison Avenue), Ryle, Jackson (now Jackson Street), Willow Pl, Harrison, Cedar, Oak Pl, Sindle Av, Van Ness Av, rock crusher, Brookside Laundry. Part 2: Great Notch section (E. Main St or Long Hill Rd, Jacobus Av, Notch Rd, Erie Greenwood Lake branch), turned about 67 degrees; anchored on Jacobus / Long Hill only.

sheet-7-2.description: The right-hand part of sheet 7 is the Great Notch section at the eastern end of the township, drawn turned so that north points up and to the right. E. Main St. or Long Hill Road runs down the right side of the part, bends at the Notch Road junction and runs off towards the lower left, and Jacobus Avenue curves in from the left to meet it. The Erie Railroad's Greenwood Lake branch crosses the lower part diagonally, with the passenger station beside Notch Road. The ground is thinly built: scattered frame dwellings and outbuildings in large lots (blocks 123, 129, 134 and 138), a shingle shed, a hotel near the station, and open land. Between the heavy dividing line and the railroad, the tract on the left holds a quarry with a narrow-gauge track, a rock crusher, engine and boiler houses, a dynamite store, sheds and a wood bridge. A large compass rose is drawn in block 129.
notes: Placed from one junction (Jacobus Avenue / Long Hill Road) with the scale of the atlas and the rotation from its measured lines (67 degrees); low confidence.
The drawn Long Hill Road / Notch Road junction does not match the modern one (about 25 m difference); the road and the grade crossing appear to have been rebuilt.

sheet-8-1.description: The upper part of sheet 8 shows the eastern edge of the Little Falls centre, where Main Street becomes E. Main St. or Long Hill Road. On the left Lincoln Avenue and 1st Avenue run down to Stanley, with the Mack Molding Co. works and dwellings in block 81, and Maple Avenue runs up to the top left corner. The abandoned Morris Canal and its tow path cross the part diagonally, with Wilmore Road, the old Cedar Grove Avenue, beside it, and 2nd and 3rd Avenues ending at Wilmore Road. Van Ness Avenue runs up past block 89 along the Peckman River. Along E. Main St. stand the Service Printing Co. and Mercury Radio Co., Chester J. Hunt Inc., importers of bulbs and seeds, and a row of frame dwellings, and the mill race of the Little Falls Washing Co. joins the Peckman River at the right, where the washing works stand. A heavy line separates this part from the lower part of the sheet.
notes: E. Main Street or Long Hill Road is today's E. Main Street at this point.
Only four control points were detected; Lincoln / Main, Main / Maple and E. Main / Van Ness were not.

Main St or Long Hill Rd, Lincoln Av, 1st Av, Stanley, Maple Av, Van Ness Av, Wilmore Rd along the Morris Canal, Little Falls Washing Co on the Peckman River. Part 2 (lower, further east): Long Hill Rd, Cedar Grove Rd, Randolph Pl, Hudson, Browertown Rd, Lower Notch Rd, public school no. 2.

sheet-8-2.description: The lower part of sheet 8 continues E. Main St. or Long Hill Road eastwards from the Peckman River towards Great Notch. Cedar Grove Road runs down the left side beside the Peckman River, Randolph Place and Hudson form a small subdivision of narrow lots south of the main road (blocks 126, 127 and 128), and on the right Browertown Road and Lower Notch Road meet the main road on either side of the abandoned Morris Canal. Little Falls Public School No. 2 stands on the main road at the right, and the rest of the part is thinly built with frame dwellings, some with outbuildings, in large lots; much of the ground south of the road is open (blocks 128 and 129).
notes: The two Cedar Grove Road junctions were hand-picked; the detector paired lines on the river side of the road.
E. Main Street / Randolph Place was left out (12 m residual); the remaining fit is weak (3.8 m RMSE) and the fitted scale is about 3 percent large.
